scenes.text: Everyone describes it as a door. Something opening. Something arriving from outside you.
scenes.query: A heavy door swings slowly open into a bright empty hallway.

scenes.text: The leading model says the opposite. Nothing arrives. Something gets turned down.
scenes.query: A hand turns a physical dimmer dial downward and the room darkens evenly.

scenes.text: Right now your brain is not receiving this room. It is predicting it.
scenes.query: A camera lens racks focus across an ordinary room until every detail resolves.

scenes.text: Prediction is cheaper than perception. So your brain guesses, then checks the guess against the signal.
scenes.query: A wireframe outline of a chair fills in with color and texture until it looks real.

scenes.text: And it trusts its own guesses enormously. It has to. That trust is what holds the room still.
scenes.query: A completely still room held in a locked camera frame while dust drifts in the light.

scenes.text: Carhart-Harris and Friston named this REBUS. Psychedelics, they propose, relax that trust.
scenes.query: A scientific paper page turns under a desk lamp and one passage is underlined in pencil.

scenes.text: Call it a filter easing off. But hear the word filter as metaphor, not anatomy.

scenes.text: What floods in was never far away. It was being subtracted, quietly, every second of your life.
scenes.query: Daylight floods into a dim room as heavy curtains are drawn fully open.

scenes.text: Which reframes the whole experience. You did not travel anywhere. Subtraction paused.
scenes.query: A person stands perfectly still on a moving walkway as the corridor slides past them.

scenes.text: And if it is a dial rather than a door, chemistry is not the only hand on it.
scenes.query: Several different hands reach in one after another and adjust the same control knob.

scenes.text: Grief moves it. Standing in front of something enormous moves it.
scenes.query: A small figure stands at the base of an enormous cliff face and looks upward.

scenes.text: Forty uncomfortable minutes of sitting still moves it.
scenes.query: A person sits cross-legged on a bare floor, completely still, as afternoon light shifts across them.

scenes.text: Being genuinely surprised, which is rarer than you think, moves it.
scenes.query: A still pond surface is broken suddenly by a single unexpected falling drop.

scenes.text: Here is the honest part. We can measure a noisier brain under these compounds.
scenes.query: An oscilloscope screen fills with dense irregular waveform activity in a dark lab.

scenes.text: Whether noisier means truer is still an open fight among the people who study it.
scenes.query: Two researchers at a whiteboard disagree, erasing and rewriting the same diagram.

scenes.text: Signal diversity is not the same as seeing more clearly. Hold that loosely.
scenes.query: Two nearly identical printed charts are laid side by side and carefully compared.

scenes.text: So come back to the room you are actually sitting in.
scenes.query: A slow push through a doorway into an ordinary lived-in living room at dusk.

scenes.text: Your hands. The light on the wall. The sound underneath the sound.
scenes.query: Close details of an ordinary room: a mug, a cable, light moving slowly on a plain wall.

scenes.text: All of it already ran the same filter, at a setting you never chose.
scenes.query: A dimmer dial is raised again and warm light returns evenly across a plain wall.

scenes.text: So when did the world last come off like a skin, and what were you doing right before?
scenes.query: A person looks at their own open hand in daylight as if seeing it for the first time.
